info.name: MessMate API
info.description:
MessMate - Smart Mess & Shared Housing Management Platform.

Live: https://messmatebackend.vercel.app (default)
For a local server set the `baseUrl` collection variable to `http://localhost:5000`.

Verified against the live deployment: 83 passed, 0 failed, 8 manual (file uploads, OTP paste, and the bKash hosted page).

## How to use

1. Run the three requests in **Auth / Login** first. Each one saves its own token into a collection variable (`adminToken`, `managerToken`, `memberToken`), so every later request is already authenticated for the right role.
2. Run **Mess / Create mess** as the manager - it saves `messId`.
3. Run **Member / Add member** then **Member / Get mess members** - the list saves `memberId`.
4. The **Error cases** folder is the three-role demo: every request there is expected to fail, with the status noted in its name.

## Seeded accounts

| Role | Email |
|---|---|
| ADMIN | admin@messmate.app |
| MESS_MANAGER | manager@messmate.app |
| MEMBER | member@messmate.app |

Passwords come from the environment file used at deploy time.

## Registration is two step

`POST /auth/register` does not create the account. It mails a six digit OTP and parks the signup in Redis for five minutes. `POST /auth/verify-email` with that code creates the user and returns tokens. Use the seeded accounts above for everything else, so you do not have to open a mailbox.

## Response shape

Success: `{ success, statusCode, message, data, meta? }`
Error: `{ success, statusCode, message, errors: [] }`

request.description: Confirms the API is up. Returns the standard success envelope.

item.description: **Running this folder repeatedly:** /api/v1/auth is rate limited to 30 requests per 15 minutes, much tighter than the 300 everything else gets, because login and register are the brute-force targets. A full collection run spends about eight of those, so three runs back to back start answering 429. That is the limiter working, not a broken collection - wait out the window.

item.name: User
item.description: Profile and profile image. The image is optional throughout - avatarUrl and avatarPublicId are nullable, and an account with no picture is normal.

request.description: Name and phone only. Email, role and status are not editable here - changing a role is an admin action, not a profile edit.

**Manual step** - a real file has to be picked in the Body tab, so a collection run skips this one.

Replacing a picture deletes the previous file, but only after the new one is saved - doing it first would leave the account with no picture if the upload then failed.

In Postman: Body tab -> form-data -> key `avatar`, change the type dropdown from Text to File, then pick an image.

**Manual step** - only works after the upload above, which needs a file picked by hand.

item.name: Cycle
item.description: One billing cycle = one calendar month of one mess. OPEN while meals, expenses, deposits and grocery duty are recorded; close-cycle runs the settlement and CLOSES it.

exec: // The cutoff demo further down has to aim at a date the member has already
// joined for. Today is the only one that qualifies: anything earlier trips
// the join-date guard first and answers 400 instead of the 409 it means to show.

request.description: Only one cycle may be OPEN per mess at a time. Saves `cycleId` automatically.
Paginated, filterable by status and year.
Includes a live summary: running meal count, grocery total and meal rate while the cycle is still OPEN.

The graded core: computes the meal rate, splits every shared expense, prorates rent by tenure, credits deposits and self-paid expenses, and writes one MemberBill per member. Uses a conditional update so firing this twice at once yields one 200 and one 409, never two sets of bills.
Deletes the generated bills and reopens the month. Refused once any bill has a payment against it.

item.name: Meal
item.description: The daily register: how many lunches and dinners each member actually ate. This is what the settlement charges for - see Meal Plan for what members declare in advance.

request.description: One call records the whole mess for one day. Re-sending the same member+date is a correction (upsert), not a duplicate - and restores a soft-deleted entry instead of erroring on the unique constraint. Refused once the cycle is CLOSED.
Readable by the whole mess - the register is the wall chart everyone checks. Filter by `date` or `memberId`.
The ledger page this project replaces: every member's lunch/dinner/total, the mess total, and the running meal rate (grocery so far / meals so far).
Refused once the cycle is CLOSED.
Soft delete - the row stays so the unique slot is preserved and re-recording the same day restores it rather than duplicating.

item.name: Meal Plan
item.description: What a member declares they will eat, ahead of time, so whoever is on grocery duty knows the headcount. Declaring for a day closes at 11 PM Dhaka time the night before - the 4th must be declared by 11 PM on the 3rd, never on the 4th itself.

item.name: Set my plan (Member) - before the cutoff

request.description: A member plans only for themselves; a manager may name someone else via `memberId`, or omit it to plan their own meals - the manager lives in the mess too. Pick dates a few days out so the 11 PM cutoff has not passed yet.

item.name: 409 - set my plan after the cutoff

request.description:
Planning for today is always past its own cutoff - the deadline was 11 PM Dhaka time last night. Returns 409 naming the exact deadline that was missed.

The date comes from `{{lateDate}}`, set to today by the Open cycle script, because a hard-coded past date would trip the join-date guard instead and answer 400.
Every day of the month, planned or not, each marked isLocked so a client can grey out days that can no longer be changed.
Open to the whole mess, not just the manager: whoever is on grocery duty needs the day's headcount to shop correctly.
Copies one day's declarations into the actual MealEntry register as a starting point. Never overwrites an entry that already exists - a correction the manager already made is not undone.

item.name: Expense
item.description: Every cost of the month. GROCERY sets the meal rate; everything except GROCERY and RENT is a shared cost split EQUAL or BY_MEAL; RENT is prorated by tenure at settlement.

request.description: The receipt photo is optional - most expenses are entered from memory. This request has no file, so it is plain JSON.

**Manual step** - a real file has to be picked in the Body tab, so a collection run skips this one.

Multipart form-data with a file in the `receipt` field, uploaded to Cloudinary. In Postman: Body -> form-data -> key `receipt` -> change type from Text to File.
Readable by everyone in the mess - these are the exact numbers each member is about to be billed from. Filter by `type`, `paidByMemberId`, or `searchTerm`.
Grouped the way the settlement uses it: grocery total, rent, shared total, running meal rate, and who has paid for what (their settlement credit).
Refused once the cycle is CLOSED. A new receipt file replaces the old one only after the upload succeeds; the old Cloudinary file is then deleted.
Audited as EXPENSE_DELETED - removing an expense changes what every member in the mess owes.

item.name: Grocery Duty
item.description: Works like a booking system: the manager books one member for a date range of any length - four days for one person, six for the next - the same way a hotel booking picks check-in and check-out. There is no auto-generator; the calendar is built one booking at a time.

request.description: Any member of the mess, any date range inside the cycle month, any length. Rejected with 409 if it overlaps an existing booking - two people cannot both be on duty the same day.
Readable by the whole mess. The bookings as ranges, in date order.

item.name: Get cycle calendar - day by day

request.description: The same bookings expanded to one row per calendar day, with unbooked days marked null - what a calendar UI renders directly.
Answers 'this month, how many days did I do?' for the caller - total days plus the individual bookings they came from. Works for the manager too, since they have a membership in their own mess.
Swap the member or change the dates. Re-checked against the month bounds and every other booking for an overlap.
Hard delete - a rota entry carries no financial history the way a meal or an expense does.

item.name: Deposit
item.description: Cash a member hands the manager during the month, before any bill exists. Becomes settlement credit automatically - see the dueAmount drop in Cycle / Close cycle after adding one.

request.description: Refused once the cycle is CLOSED.
Readable by everyone in the mess - this is what lets a member confirm the cash they handed over actually got recorded. Filter by `memberId`.
Refused once the cycle is CLOSED.
Audited as DEPOSIT_DELETED - removing it takes credit away from whoever it belonged to.

item.name: Payment
item.description:
bKash tokenized checkout against a settled bill.

The amount always comes from the bill row, never from the request body. The callback is a public GET whose query string arrives through the user's browser, so nothing it claims is believed: every callback calls bKash's execute endpoint and settles only when the reply says statusCode 0000, transactionStatus Completed, currency BDT and an amount matching the row we created. Settlement runs behind a conditional update, so a browser refresh that fires the callback three times still credits the bill once.

Actually paying requires opening the returned paymentUrl in a browser and completing the sandbox wallet flow - that part cannot be automated, and it is what the demo video shows.

item.name: Close cycle (Manager) - bills are what payment needs

request.description: Payment has nothing to act on until settlement has produced a bill. The Cycle folder reopened this month so the meal, expense, duty and deposit folders could write to it; closing it again here regenerates the bills the requests below pay against.

Where a member finds the billId they hand to create-payment. One row per cycle: meal count, meal cost, shared cost, prorated rent, credit from deposits and self-paid expenses, and what is left to pay.

A negative dueAmount is not an error - it means this member fronted more grocery money than they ate, and the mess owes them.

exec: const mine = res?.data?.find((b) => b.cycle?.id === cycleId && Number(b.dueAmount) > 0);

item.name: Get my bills (Manager) - the manager gets one too

request.description:
The manager lives in the mess like everyone else: they eat the meals, take their turn at the grocery run, and settlement bills them the same way. Managing is extra responsibility, not a different kind of residency.

Saves the manager's bill id so the 403 below has something real to aim at.

item.name: Create payment (Member) - starts a real bKash checkout

request.description:
The body carries only the bill id. The amount is read from the bill row - an amount arriving from the client is how a member pays 1 taka against a 4000 taka bill.

The Payment row is created and committed before bKash is called, never inside the transaction: a network round trip holding a database connection open dies with the gateway. If the call then fails the row simply stays UNPAID, which is the correct record of what happened.

Returns a real sandbox paymentUrl. Open it in a browser to actually pay; bKash then sends the browser to the callback.

Every checkout attempt this member has made, across every mess they live in. A bill can have several: an abandoned try, then a real one. Only rows in PAID carry a bkashTrxId, and that field is the evidence that money actually moved.
Someone else's payment is a 403 even with a perfectly valid token for the same mess.

item.name: 302 - callback with a paymentID we never issued

request.description:
`status=success` in the query string is a rumour that arrived through someone's address bar. The service looks the paymentID up, finds nothing it issued, and settles nothing.

It still redirects rather than erroring - every callback path does, because a member who really paid must never be shown a failure. Turn off Settings -> Automatically follow redirects to see the 302 itself.

item.name: 403 - pay a bill that is not yours

request.description: Two separate questions get asked: is this caller in that mess at all, and is this particular bill theirs. A valid token for the mess answers only the first.

item.name: 404 - pay a bill that does not exist

request.description: A well-formed id that belongs to nothing.

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Platform administration — everything here is ADMIN only, because none of it is about one mess.

The two state-changing pairs (role there and back, block then unblock) are deliberately round trips: leaving the demo member promoted or blocked would break every request after this folder. If a run stops between the two halves of a pair, re-run the second half by hand.

request.description:
Platform health in one call: users by role, blocked count, messes and active memberships, open and closed cycles, and the money — deposits taken, expenses recorded, payments actually settled through bKash, and what is still outstanding across every unpaid bill.

Every figure is a count or a sum with an index behind it, and they run together rather than in sequence. A dashboard that costs ten round trips is a dashboard nobody opens.

item.name: Get all users - search, sort, paginate

request.description:
`searchTerm` matches name or email case-insensitively. Passwords are never selected, so they cannot leak through this route even by accident.

Saves the three demo user ids the requests below act on.

item.name: Get all users - filter by role and status

request.description: The same endpoint narrowed by role and account status. Soft-deleted users are excluded from every variation.

item.name: Get single user - with their messes

request.description: Returns the messes this user manages and the memberships they hold, because that is what an admin needs before acting: a manager with an open month and a member with an unpaid bill are not the same person to act on.

Writes a `USER_ROLE_CHANGED` audit row carrying the before and after role. The role is read from the database on every request, not from the token, so the change takes effect on the user's very next call without them logging in again.
The other half of the round trip. Leaving the demo member promoted would change what every request after this folder is allowed to do.
A blocked account is refused at login and on every authenticated request, since the middleware checks the database row rather than trusting the token. Writes a `USER_BLOCKED` audit row.
Writes `USER_UNBLOCKED`. Run this even if you ran the block by hand — every request below this folder logs in as that member.

item.name: Get audit logs - the trail, filtered

request.description:
Everything money- or permission-shaped is written here as it happens — cycle closed and reopened, member removed, expense and deposit deleted, payment settled, role changed, user blocked and unblocked — each with the actor and the before/after state.

Filterable by `action`, `entity`, `entityId` and `actorId`. A log that is written but never readable is only half a feature; this is the other half.

item.name: 403 - an admin cannot change their own role

request.description: Self-demotion would lock the platform's last way in. The same guard covers blocking yourself.

item.name: 409 - demote a manager who still owns a mess

request.description:
A demoted manager keeps owning the mess row but loses every route that maintains it — the month could no longer be closed and the ledger would sit there unfinishable. Hand the mess over or delete it first.

The matching rule for blocking: a manager cannot be blocked while one of their messes has an OPEN cycle, because nobody else can record the meals or close it.

item.name: Error cases (three role demo)
item.description: Every request here is expected to FAIL. The status code is in the name. This folder is the role isolation demonstration.

request.description: Blocked by auth(Role.ADMIN).

item.name: 403 - Member tries to create a mess
403 - Member tries to update their own mess

request.description: Belonging to a mess is not permission to edit it. This is the second authorization layer: auth() lets the request in, checkMessAccess and the role check inside the service stop it.

item.name: 403 - Manager B touches Manager A mess

request.description: Register a second manager, create a mess with them, then paste that mess id here. checkMessAccess returns 403 - the whole point of the second authorization layer.
Returns every failing rule as a separate { field, message } entry in `errors`, not just the first one.

item.name: 400 - role escalation blocked at the schema

request.description: ADMIN is absent from the register enum, so no request can create one. Admins exist only through the seeder.
Send this twice. The second call returns 409.

item.name: 400 - admin cannot be a mess member
Cleanup
item.description: Runs last, and in this exact order for a reason. Removing a member is refused while they still owe money, and deleting a mess is refused while any cycle is still OPEN - two rules that pull in opposite directions, so the cycle is reopened, the member released, and the cycle closed again before the mess goes.

item.name: Reopen cycle (Admin) - clears the generated bills

request.description:
Removing a member is refused while they have an unpaid bill, and closing the month is what generated that bill. Reopening deletes the bills so the settlement can be regenerated, which also releases the member.

Refused outright once a payment has actually settled against the month - at that point the ledger has left the building, and rewriting it would contradict a real bKash transaction. Abandoned checkout attempts go with the bills they belonged to; a settled one can never reach here.

Sets status LEFT with leftAt rather than deleting, so their meals and expenses stay attached to the months they belong to and rent stays prorated to the day they left.

Refuses with 409 if they still have an unpaid bill. Writes a MEMBER_REMOVED audit row inside the same transaction.

Kept in Cleanup on purpose: it sets the member to LEFT, and the duplicate-add case in Error cases expects them to still be ACTIVE. Running it earlier turns that 409 into a 201, because re-adding someone who left restores their old membership row instead of conflicting.

item.name: Close cycle (Manager) - nothing may be left OPEN

request.description: The delete below refuses while any billing cycle is still OPEN, because deleting would strand every meal and expense recorded in it. This closes the month the reopen above put back into edit.

Sets isDeleted and deletedAt - the row stays in the database. Refuses with 409 while any billing cycle is still OPEN, because deleting would strand every meal and expense recorded in it.

Kept last on purpose: it soft-deletes the mess that every Mess and Member request above depends on, so running it earlier makes the rest of the collection return 404.
